title: Weird websites, explained
fullTitle: Why Do Websites Do Weird Things? Five Glitches in One Minute

scenes.narration: You tapped Pay once. The app made two orders. Nothing you did was wrong.
captions: You tapped Pay once. The app made two orders.

scenes.narration: Websites do strange things. A page that stays old after an update. Someone else's name on your screen. A date one day off. A deleted record that still shows up.
captions: An old page after an update. Someone else's name.
A date one day off. A deleted record that still shows.

scenes.narration: Web Reality Checks explains why. Each film rebuilds one glitch as a small pretend app on a laptop, breaks it on purpose, proves the test can fail, applies the smallest fix, and tests again.
captions: Each glitch rebuilt as a small pretend app on a laptop.

scenes.narration: Take the double charge. Without a ticket number on each attempt, two attempts made two orders. With a ticket number, two attempts made one order. Thirteen tests pass in that fixture.
captions: Without a ticket number: two attempts, two orders.
With a ticket number: two attempts, one order.

scenes.narration: Every strange moment gets everyday objects: a dropped phone call, a manager waiting at the door, a library card left in the drawer.
captions: Everyday objects explain each strange moment.

scenes.narration: Everything uses made-up data on a local machine. It is not an audit of any real product, and each fix covers only the problem it shows.
captions: Not an audit of any real product.

scenes.narration: Watch the films and run the tests yourself. The repository is linked below.
captions: Watch the films. Run the tests yourself.
